title: Thin shell thickness identification from a cantilever frequency
source: Euler–Bernoulli cantilever beam theory (Timoshenko and Young, Vibration Problems in Engineering): f1=beta1²/(2 pi L²) sqrt(EI/(rho A)), beta1=1.875104068711961. For a unit-width strip with I=b t³/12 and A=b t, f1=beta1² t sqrt(E/(12 rho))/(2 pi L²).

quantities.reason: The independent thin-strip target is t=0.005 m; the coarse shell inverse starts at the nearby FE-stationary value and the 8% band covers the stated shear, rotary-inertia and mesh effects.
The closed relation is linear in t; with 1e-5 Hz independent error, sigma_t=1e-5/(f1/t), and the endpoint is t-1.959963984540054 sigma_t.
The same thin-beam linearization gives t+1.959963984540054 sigma_t.
Euler–Bernoulli thin-strip reference; the 8% allowance covers shear, rotary-inertia and coarse two-element shell effects.
